Failure mode: machine stops responding (death)
Mechanism: actuator counts p+1 ticks without a valid order and revokes the mandate (MAN-04), then auto-switches to the certified second (REL-01)
Share source: HYPOTHESIS -- share of the ECU rate spent on a hard stop
Note: Safe at system level: the second machine keeps the service.

Failure mode: machine freezes then resumes
Mechanism: same silence counter, and on thaw the stale order is dropped twice over: mandate number and tick label (MAN-08, REL-07)
Evidence: core/src/arbiter.c:54 (holder + mandate + tick accepted), core/src/arbiter.c:70 (mandate check)
Share source: HYPOTHESIS -- share of the ECU rate spent on a freeze
Note: Safe: the returning machine is disarmed by construction.

Failure mode: machine runs slow, misses ticks
Mechanism: miss counter published in every STATUT; the machine is deposed only when the misses are consecutive (DET-03)
Share source: HYPOTHESIS -- share of the ECU rate spent on slowness
Note: Safe: isolated misses are absorbed within the parameter bounds.

Failure mode: machine computes a wrong value, a certified shadow exists
Mechanism: order/shadow comparison over three ticks raises the disagreement alert (DET-09, REP-05)
Share source: HYPOTHESIS -- 90 % of the wrong-value cases happen while a shadow exists
Note: Dangerous for the value applied, but detected and alarmed.

Failure mode: machine computes a wrong value, no certified shadow
Mechanism: none: the comparison needs a certified second; without it the wrong value is applied silently
Share source: HYPOTHESIS -- 10 % of the wrong-value cases happen with no shadow
Note: The one dangerous-undetected share of the software: a third machine (vote) is the level-X answer, REP-08.

Failure mode: emitting side loses, duplicates, reorders or delays frames
Mechanism: tick label, mandate number and miss counter reject a reordered or late frame (MAN-02, DET-03, ROB-02)
Share source: HYPOTHESIS -- share of the ECU rate spent on frame handling
Note: Safe: dropped and counted, absorbed within the bounds.

Failure mode: corrupted or forged frame emitted
Mechanism: CRC-32C at level S, keyed SipHash-2-4 MAC at level C (DET-04, SEC-02)
Share source: HYPOTHESIS -- share of the ECU rate spent on corrupted frames
Note: Safe: dropped, counted, journaled, no effect on the service.

Failure mode: latent (dormant) fault, no effect until a second fault
Mechanism: none at runtime: the invariant exploration and the mutant bench are development evidence, not a runtime diagnostic
Share source: HYPOTHESIS -- share of the ECU rate spent on dormant defects
Note: Dormant: safe today, but it is what makes a second fault dangerous. It drives the latent-fault metric, not the PMHF.

Failure mode: second fault strikes before the redundancy is restored
Mechanism: the actuator counts p+1 ticks without a valid order, plays the will up to its horizon and then falls back to its own damped loop: red lamp and stop requested (ACT-02, ACT-03, DEG-05)
Evidence: core/src/control.c:165 (I6, the horizon of the will), core/src/arbiter.c:231 (the fallback loop)
Share source: COMPUTED -- lambda(ECU)^2 x the repair time; the repair time is a HYPOTHESIS (1 h)
Note: Dangerous for the goal (no fresh command) but detected: the safe state is reached and announced.

Failure mode: both machines dead
Mechanism: same path: the will covers the horizon, then the local damped loop holds the rack (ACT-02, DEG-05)
Evidence: core/src/control.c:165 (I6, the horizon of the will), core/src/arbiter.c:231 (the fallback loop)
Share source: COMPUTED -- lambda(ECU)^2 x the FTTI (lambda is a HYPOTHESIS): the two machines must die inside the horizon of the will
Note: Dangerous for the goal, detected: the safe state is reached.

Failure mode: arbitration core stops (crash, deadlock)
Mechanism: none: the actuator is a single channel, no second arbitration path at the base level (ACT-10 is the level-X extension)
Evidence: core/src/arbiter.c (one arbiter), host/safety/fta.py (F11 out of scope)
Share source: HYPOTHESIS -- share of the controller rate spent on a hard stop
Note: Single point of failure: nothing observes the arbiter but itself.

Failure mode: arbitration core computes a wrong mandate or value
Mechanism: none at runtime: the invariants are checked offline (explorer, verifier), not on the target
Share source: HYPOTHESIS -- share of the controller rate spent on a wrong computation
Note: Systematic/software defect: excluded from the random-failure budget by ISO 26262, but counted here because the honest answer is that nothing detects it at runtime.

Failure mode: position feedback path faulty (sensor and wiring on the target; simulated plant in the demonstrator)
Mechanism: none: the law trusts the measurement, no plausibility check compares the rack with the command (CMD-06 bounds the command, not the response)
Evidence: core/src/control.c:65 (error = setpoint - pos), core/src/control.c:72 (clamp of the command)
Share source: HYPOTHESIS -- share of the controller rate spent on the feedback path
Note: In the demonstrator the rack is the software plant model (core/include/relais/control.h:85); on a real target this is a sensor.

Failure mode: signalling (lamp) faulty: the degradation is not shown
Mechanism: none: no channel observes the lamp of the actuator
Share source: HYPOTHESIS -- share of the controller rate spent on signalling
Note: Safe for the actuation, but it hides the degradation from the driver.

Failure mode: journal or observer faulty: the record of the ticks is lost
Mechanism: none: the journal is an observation channel, not a barrier
Share source: HYPOTHESIS -- share of the controller rate spent on observation
Note: Safe for the actuation; it destroys the evidence of the run.

Failure mode: power or clock transient leaves the arbitration running with a corrupted state
Mechanism: none: no watchdog, no self-test of the arbitration state at the base level
Evidence: core/src/arbiter.c (no supervisory loop around the arbiter)
Share source: HYPOTHESIS -- share of the controller rate spent on transients
Note: Dangerous and silent: a watchdog is the cheapest lift.

Failure mode: power stage or motor failure: no torque is delivered
Mechanism: none: the arbiter sees a command, never the reaction of the rack
Evidence: core/src/arbiter.c:192 (the applied value), core/include/relais/control.h:85 (the plant is simulated)
Share source: HYPOTHESIS -- share of the power path rate spent on the drive
Note: Dominant term of the whole FMEDA: see the sensitivity analysis.

Failure mode: mechanical jam or excessive friction
Mechanism: none: no current, speed or position plausibility check
Evidence: core/src/control.c (no deviation check between command and rack)
Share source: HYPOTHESIS -- share of the power path rate spent on the mechanics
Note: Same blind spot as the drive failure.

Failure mode: short or insulation fault in the power path
Mechanism: none: the fault is invisible to the arbitration
Evidence: core/src/arbiter.c (no supervision of the power path)
Share source: HYPOTHESIS -- share of the power path rate spent on cabling
Note: Would also break the actuation channel itself.

Failure mode: link cut (open circuit, connector)
Mechanism: the actuator sees no order (p+1 silence) and the machine sees no STATUT after bail_ticks, so it deposes itself (DET-07, DET-08, MAN-09)
Share source: HYPOTHESIS -- share of the link rate spent on a cut
Note: Safe: the other machine keeps the service, the handover is automatic.

Failure mode: frames lost, duplicated, reordered or delayed
Mechanism: tick label, mandate number and miss counter reject a reordered or late frame (MAN-02, DET-03, ROB-02)
Share source: HYPOTHESIS -- share of the link rate spent on congestion
Note: Safe: dropped and counted, absorbed within the bounds.

Failure mode: corrupted or forged frame (EMC, ground loop)
Mechanism: CRC-32C at level S, keyed SipHash-2-4 MAC at level C (DET-04)
Share source: HYPOTHESIS -- share of the link rate spent on corrupted frames
Note: Safe: dropped, counted, journaled.

Failure mode: transceiver degraded: the frames no longer arrive but the link stays up
Mechanism: same silence path: the machine deposes itself after bail_ticks, the actuator revokes after p+1 (DET-07, MAN-04)
Share source: HYPOTHESIS -- share of the link rate spent on a silent transceiver
Note: Safe: behaves like a cut, and is detected like a cut.

Failure mode: inter-computer link cut
Mechanism: loss of ETAT declared after two ticks (DET-06); the holder keeps commanding, the redundancy is reported degraded
Share source: HYPOTHESIS -- share of the link rate spent on a cut
Note: Safe: no handover, the holder keeps the service.

Failure mode: ETAT frames lost or delayed
Mechanism: the same two-tick ETAT watchdog (DET-06)
Share source: HYPOTHESIS -- share of the link rate spent on congestion
Note: Safe: the replica ages and the redundancy is reported degraded.

Failure mode: ETAT frame corrupted
Mechanism: CRC-32C at level S, keyed MAC at level C (DET-04)
Share source: HYPOTHESIS -- share of the link rate spent on corrupted frames
Note: Safe: dropped, counted.
